title: Miquel Sirera Perelló
text:
Miquel Sirera Perelló
      PhD student, Northeastern University
      Data, Networks, and Algorithms Lab · Boston
    
  

  
    
      I'm a PhD student at Northeastern, in the Data, Networks, and Algorithms Lab.
      I work on large language models: how to run them across several machines, including small ones, and how to change something they know without retraining the whole model.
    
    
      Research
      Resume
      sirera.m@northeastern.edu
    
    NeurIPS 2026 Top Reviewer
  

  
    Work
    A few things I'm working on right now.

    
      
        Resilience for distributed language models
        This continues JARVIS, which splits a language model across several devices. We added a way for the remaining devices to cover for one that drops out. We tried it with Gemma-2B on 18 radios in the Colosseum testbed, and on seven Raspberry Pis.
      

      
        Communication-aware pruning
        Training a neural network so that, once it is split across machines, those machines have to send less to each other, without losing accuracy.
      

      
        Editing what a language model knows
        Looking for cheaper ways to correct one fact in a language model, without retraining it and without undoing everything else it already knows.
      
    
  

  
    Background
    I studied data science in Barcelona. I'm now doing a PhD in Boston.
